transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Ysolde 3 FP, Aldous 3 FP, Morwen 3 FP, Mire 3 FP. Face-up: Rising Floodwaters [H-03], The Drowned Priest [T-04].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain hammers the last stretch of the Causeway, the plank road slick and half-drowned where the water has crept up over the boards. Ahead, torches gutter under an oilcloth awning where a Warden sergeant and two spearmen check every soul crossing into Hollowmoot — packs searched, names taken, coin demanded, and anyone with a cough or a rash held back behind a rope line for the quarantine bell. Beyond them the town itself rises on its pilings out of the flood, lantern-lit and loud with the noise of too many people crammed onto too little dry ground. Somewhere out past the rooftops, faint and wrong, you can almost hear it — a thin, ragged hum riding under the rain, gone if you listen straight at it.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Warden sergeant, what's the word? Plague scare, or something stranger? We're just travelers needing through to Hollowmoot.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps up to the checkpoint's rope line, taking in the guards' postures and the huddled figures in quarantine beyond. She keeps her bearing calm and straightforward—a working cook, nothing remarkable. Her eyes flick toward the town's rooftops where that wrongness seems to settle.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: That humming — the rain's all wrong. Something's drowning that shouldn't be.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous halts at the checkpoint's edge and tilts his scarred face up into the downpour. His eyes track the strange spiral patterns of the rainfall, the way each drop catches the torchlight in stuttering rhythms that match that terrible humming beneath the rain. He stands still, reading the water like words in a book, his body tense with the weight of the omen.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Sergeant Coll, isn't it? Morwen, Order of Exorcists. I need to know what's driven you to the quarantine line—and more than that, what that sound is on the wind. That's not just rain and fear I'm hearing.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (I approach the checkpoint without hesitation, water streaming from my exorcist's coat. My eyes move from the sergeant to the rope line and the cowering refugees beyond, reading the panic and sickness there, then back to him. I'm listening—not just to his words, but to that thin hum beneath the rain, trying to place it.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: That sound—those are voices. Chanting. The Drowned Priest's congregation has to be moving toward the town, maybe already inside it.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire halts short of the checkpoint, her attention snagged by the eerie humming that rides beneath the storm. Her years in the Order's orphanage taught her to recognize ritual chanting, and her spine goes rigid—that's voices, many voices in unison, growing clearer the closer you listen. She closes her eyes, filtering out the rain, triangulating the sound's direction and proximity to Hollowmoot's pilings.)

transcript.text: Aldous stands rigid in the downpour, and for one dizzying moment the rain seems to fall in time with the hum — spiraling, deliberate, wrong. He blinks it away, shaken. "The water's not just falling," he mutters. "It's answering something. The dead don't lie still out there — the Drowned are Restless, and that sound's calling them." Beside him Mire keeps her eyes shut a moment longer, sorting thread from thread, until the noise resolves into something unmistakable: not wind, not birds, but throats — dozens of them, chanting in ragged unison, and close. "Voices," she says grimly. "That's a congregation, not a storm." Warden Sergeant Coll's jaw tightens at the mention; his spearmen shift their grips, and he still hasn't answered Ysolde's question — he's just gained two more reasons not to want this conversation getting louder.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Sergeant, we hear the same voices you do. That's not the plague out there. Talk to me—what do we need to know?

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps toward Coll, casual but purposeful, keeping her hands empty and her posture open. She reads the angle of his jaw, the tension in his shoulders, the way his fingers grip his spear—all the small tells of a man carrying a weight he's been ordered not to set down. She meets his eyes with the calm recognition of someone who's heard frightened soldiers talk in the dark many times before.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Sergeant, you know what's coming—I can read it in how your men grip their spears. That sound in the rain isn't wind. It's the Drowned Priest gathering his flock, and the dead are answering. So tell us what we're walking into, or get out of the way.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps directly in front of Coll, his water-slicked face hard with certainty. He uses everything he's read in the omens to cut through the sergeant's defenses and force an answer out of him—not asking anymore, but demanding the truth.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Sergeant, I need to know what you've seen in that town. Not for reports or the Wardens' politics—because that sound means something specific, and people will die if we don't understand what's calling in the rain.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps closer through the rain, reading the fear in Coll's shoulders, the way his men grip their spears. She's seen this terror before—the kind that comes from knowing something's terribly wrong but having no words for it. She lowers her voice to cut through the downpour, meeting his eyes with the steady calm of someone trained to face horrors and come through whole.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Sergeant, that's a congregation—dozens of voices in unison. You know what that means. How close are they, and how many people do you have holding this checkpoint?

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire walks up to Sergeant Coll with the easy confidence of someone who's done this work. She keeps her hands visible and her voice level, soldier to soldier.)

transcript.text: Something in Coll gives way. He's held this line eleven months without a night's proper sleep, and Ysolde's quiet steadiness, Aldous's unrelenting certainty, and Morwen's calm authority together crack the weight he's been carrying alone. He waves his spearmen back a pace and drops his voice so the quarantine line won't hear. "Three nights running the chanting's come closer," he admits, rain running off his chin. "Two of my own men are behind that rope now — caught the hive two days back, wouldn't say how. The Order's gone silent on us, won't send anyone past the temple gate. And the Priest's flock — they're not out in the marsh anymore. They're *in* Hollowmoot, some of them, walking around free as you like, and nobody knows who." He steps aside from the rope line, jaw tight. "Go on through. But watch who you trust in there — and if that sound gets louder tonight, the bell's going to ring, and I won't be able to stop what happens after." He lets you pass without the coin toll, too tired or too grateful to bother collecting it, and Hollowmoot's crowded, lantern-lit sprawl opens up ahead on its groaning pilings — noisy, wet, and watching.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Mire sheltered in the abandoned mill years ago during one of the worst early floods—she was freshly badged then, still trying to understand what holding the line truly meant. The miller's daughter Sella gave her shelter when nowhere else would take her. Later, when Sella's younger siblings fell sick and the quarantine bells started to ring, Mire helped her hide them here in the loft. That bond doesn't break in the marsh.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Sella trusted me once when it cost her. She'll trust me again. The loft is the highest ground we have—that's where we go, and we move fast.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire accepts the compel on 'An Abandoned Mill'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: Sella, keeper of the old mill's grain loft, shoves through the checkpoint crowd into the lantern-light — soaked to the bone, shawl clutched tight, eyes wild with panic. begs the party to go to she begs the party to go to the old grain mill hunched in the shadow of the Warden watchtower, where the rising flood has already swallowed the ground floor., because her son followed the swarm-song into the belltower.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Sella grabs Mire's sleeve with both hands, shaking so hard her teeth click, and doesn't let go even when a Warden spearman moves to pull her back. "You remember the mill," she gets out. "You remember me. Tomas — my boy — he's been hearing that sound for a week, said it was singing to him, and tonight he went. I couldn't stop him, I couldn't—" Her voice breaks. The old grain mill squats in the watchtower's shadow, its ground floor already black and swallowed by the flood, only the loft and the sagging belltower rising clear of the water — and from up there, faint under the rain, that same ragged humming curls down toward the checkpoint. Sella won't go herself; she can't swim that current and won't leave the other little ones behind at the rope line. She just holds Mire's hands and waits for an answer.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Your boy's still in there—still himself. He can be reached before that sound takes him all the way. We move to the mill, we move now, and we don't let that water or that chanting pull any of us under.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward and takes Sella's other shoulder, her weathered hands steady against the woman's shaking frame. She reads the depths of Sella's fear—not just the worry of a mother, but the guilt of a woman who couldn't hold back her own child from something calling to him. Ysolde has heard these confessions before, in the dark galley of a night-barge when crew members unburdened themselves to the cook who wouldn't judge.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Tomas is already caught in the Drowned's pull—the sound won't let him go now. The mill's high ground, and I can read what the water's trying to tell us. We move fast, before that bell rings and Coll can't protect us anymore.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous turns from Sella directly toward the mill's distant silhouette. He steps into the downpour, tilting his scarred face up briefly to read the rain's pattern one more time—tracking the flood's current with the eye of someone who's learned to swim these waters. He doesn't hesitate at the edge of the torchlight; he's already moving toward the shadow of the watchtower and the mill beyond it.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Sella, we'll get him. That sound is calling him, but we can reach him before he's gone. I know the rites. Show us the way.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps through the checkpoint crowd to Sella, placing both hands on the woman's shoulders. Her eyes are steady—the look of someone who has faced drowning in the swamp and come through whole. "Sella, we will get him down from there. I've brought people back from the edge of the swarm-song before—Tomas isn't lost yet. Not while we can reach him." She releases Sella's shoulders and turns to Ysolde, Aldous, and Mire, reading their readiness in their faces. Then the Exorcist of Hollowmoot starts moving toward the mill, her exorcist's coat streaming water, already running through the prayers in her head—the ones the Order taught her and the stranger rites she learned in the Sallowmere's deepest places. This is what she does. This is what she was born for.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Sella, I promised you once—I'm promising again. We go to the mill, we get Tomas out, and we hold that high ground.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steadies Sella with firm hands, then turns to the party and points toward the mill's silhouette against the watchtower. She moves toward the flooded bank, ready to lead them across the current.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: No—no, I've read it wrong. The water's moving wrong. It's not safe. It's *not* safe—

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The words die in Aldous's throat as the bank drops away beneath the torchlight — and the flood answers him, a sudden surge of black water sheeting off the mill's ruined footings, faster and higher than any of you read a moment ago. He plants both boots at the water's edge, breath gone shallow, one hand white-knuckled on a piling; whatever he's seen in the rain has him back on the deck of a barge that never made it to shore, and for a long beat he can't make his legs carry him past the deep water's edge. Sella lets out a small, wrecked sound behind you — not urging, just terrified — as somewhere above, past the belltower's black silhouette, the chanting hitches, rises, and Tomas's voice threads through it, thin and wrong. Ysolde's hand finds Aldous's shoulder; Morwen's already scanning the current for a line that doesn't run through the deepest channel; Mire keeps her eyes on the loft window where a shape moves against a guttering lantern. The mill is close now — close enough to see the water climbing its stone flank — but the ground between you and it is no longer the safe wade any of you expected.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Aldous, look at me. That's Tomas up there—he's still himself, and that water won't take us if we move smart. We go together.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde's hand tightens on Aldous's shoulder, holding him in the present moment. She waits for his eyes to find hers, reads the terror running through him, and doesn't flinch from it. Then she turns both their bodies toward the water, already reading the current's pattern—the place where the mill's stone footings break the worst of the surge. "The flood's faster than we thought, but it channels around the loft pilings. We follow that line, we stay close, and we move now, before that bell rings and someone else decides Tomas isn't worth saving.")

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The dead are with me in this water. I can read the current—there's a way through, and I'm taking it now.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous grips Ysolde's steady hand and forces his scarred face up into the rain, reading the rainfall's pattern to find safe passage—invoking "Reads omens in the rainfall" [AL-01]. Terror constricts his chest, but the drowned ghosts pulse in his blood; his legs drive forward, one step into the flood then another, guided by omens written in every falling drop as he wades toward the mill.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: The flood's got a pattern like everything else here. We cross where the reeds mark it, not where the channel runs deepest—and Aldous, look at me. You're steady. Follow me to stone and living green, and we bring the boy down.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps to the water's edge, eyes narrowed against the rain. She traces the flood's spiral with one weathered hand, reading it the way the reed-folk taught her—not as random chaos, but as a rhythm with patterns and safe passages. The old marsh-prayers slip from her lips, not Order rites but something older that the Sallowmere recognizes. She finds it: the line where the current bends, where the channel's teeth turn sideways, where the reeds mark a ford that holds. "This way," she calls, pointing. "The fastest water's to the left—we cross where the reeds are thickest, where the mill's stones break its teeth. The water can't pull what holds to stone and reed-root.")

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I know this place. The waterwheel breaks the current—we move together, one behind the other. Aldous, come on. Hold the line.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps into the water and grabs Aldous by the shoulder, pulling him forward with the casual strength of someone who's crossed flooded ground her whole life. She knows this mill like her own heartbeat—knows where the waterwheel breaks the current, where the shallow ford runs beneath the tower's shadow. She leads them onward, reading the water's shape by memory of a hundred crossings, calling back: "One behind the other. Steady.")

transcript.text: The flood tries to take them and fails. Aldous reads the rain like scripture, calling out the exact heartbeat when the surge will slacken, and the drowned-ghost sense that usually paralyzes him instead becomes a compass — he crosses clean, eyes wide and startled at his own steadiness. Morwen's reed-and-stone line holds true, the current breaking harmlessly against the mill's old footings exactly where she said it would, and the path she's marked stays open behind them, a thread of calmer water the others can trust (Safe Crossing Through the Current holds on the rail). Mire hauls Aldous the last few strides with the ease of a hundred remembered crossings, planting them all against the waterwheel's dead bulk with barely a stumble, water sluicing off stone. Above them, the mill's grain loft juts out over the flood, lantern-glow flickering behind a shuttered window — and past it, higher still, the belltower's black silhouette, where the chanting has curdled into something almost like a boy's voice, thin and wrong, weaving through the swarm-song. They've crossed the water. Now there's a locked loft, a missing boy, and a sound climbing the tower stairs to meet them.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Tomas! Your mother sent us, boy—fight that sound and listen to my voice. You're still yourself up there, and we're coming for you.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward against the mill's stone, squaring her shoulders toward the belltower. She raises her voice to carry through the rain and chanting, projecting it like she's calling crew to gather in the dark galley of a night-barge. As she speaks, she listens—reads the thin thread where Tomas's own voice still lives within the swarm-song, and aims her words at that place where the boy is still fighting to stay himself.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The drowned are with me—and they won't let the Priest have him. I'm cutting that thread now.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous throws himself back against the waterwheel's stone, rain-slicked face turned upward toward the belltower. The ghost-sense that usually breaks him has become a weapon, and he speaks with voices layered beneath his own—calling out to every soul drowned in the Sallowmere, using their screaming refusal to shatter the Drowned Priest's hold on Tomas, trying to break the chanting before the boy is pulled any higher.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: The sound climbs toward him, but I stand against it. These rites are older than Order, older than the hive itself—and the marsh knows them.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen plants herself against the waterwheel's stone, raising her voice in the older prayers—the ones before the Order's formal rites, the marsh-songs that the Sallowmere itself understands. Her hands move in the old signs, drawing a circle of will and word around them, creating a warded space where the swarm-song's pull grows thin and Tomas might still hear his own voice beneath the choir's hunger.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I know these boards. Tomas is up there. I'm through.

ambiguities.issue: The Story Pile draw (PS-16) happens *after* the compel (event 39) is already narrated and accepted. The rule says 'the complication must involve the drawn NPC or move the drawn thread,' but the complication's content was fixed before the card was known, so the drawn card cannot literally shape the complication that already occurred.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table treated the requirement as prospective: PS-16 is expected to be woven into the scene's ongoing/following fiction rather than into the already-narrated compel text itself.

ambiguities.section: §6A (Draw triggers table, row: "A player accepts a compel that did not come from a deck draw")
ambiguities.issue: The rule fires a mandatory Story Pile draw when a non-deck compel is accepted, and requires the complication to 'involve the drawn NPC or move the drawn thread.' In this scene the compel (event 83, tag 'No clan will shelter me' on YS-01, an improvised NPC 'Ket') was fully proposed and accepted before the triggered pile draw (events 85-86, PS-14) happened. The spec never says whether the pile draw should occur before the compel is framed (so its content can shape the compel) or strictly after acceptance as a bookkeeping consequence. As logged, the draw came after the complication was already narrated, so PS-14's content had no chance to inform 'Ket' or the accepted complication.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table treated the draw as a post-hoc formality: PS-14 was revealed and placed face-up on the rail after acceptance, without altering or being referenced by the already-narrated complication.

ambiguities.issue: The Add rule says a newly-mattering NPC 'goes to a player's pile if it ties to one character, otherwise to the GM Story Pile,' but the log does not record which pile received SN-03 ('Reed-Warden Ket'), and it is unclear whether Ket ties specifically to Ysolde (via the exile backstory surfaced in the compel) or is a general-world NPC belonging in the GM pile.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Card was logged as added (event 93, draw_id SN-03) with no pile field; destination left unrecorded/unresolved at the table.

ambiguities.issue: T-02 left play at event 105 (Aldous's success-with-style overcome, event 103), but Mire's overcome roll at event 109 still lists target_card T-02 and resolves it as a success, effectively 'overcoming' a card that had already left play four events earlier. The spec does not define how the engine should handle multiple actors' rolls declared in parallel (events 98–101) against a single GM obstacle when one actor's resolution removes that obstacle before the others resolve.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated T-02 as a stale fictional label for the shared 'read the crust pattern' task rather than a still-extant rail card; Mire's roll was scored as a normal overcome against the surviving passive opposition (H-03's tag), with no second removal or double-award of T-02's leave-play effects.

ambiguities.section: §3 outcome table vs. Fate Core baseline for Create Advantage ties
ambiguities.issue: Event 107 is a Create Advantage roll that ties. The §3 table says all ties are 'success at a minor cost' with a deck draw, but Fate Core baseline (the stated rules baseline) normally resolves a Create Advantage tie as a boost (1 free invoke, self-expiring), not as a full 'success.' The spec doesn't say whether the deck-draw minor-cost mechanic stacks on top of the boost-tie handling for CA specifically, or replaces it.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Applied both: the tie produced a boost-style aspect with 1 free invoke (per Fate Core baseline) AND triggered the §3 minor-cost deck draw, resolved via the §4 drawn-player-card compel procedure since the drawn card (PX-07) belonged to a player.

ambiguities.issue: Across events 102, 103 and 109, the opposition (+2) is attributed to H-03's tag ('hides the drowned dead'), while the target_card field names T-02 as the card being overcome. The rules don't specify whether the card recorded as 'overcome' (§8's leave-play trigger) must be the same card whose tag actually set the passive opposition, or whether a different face-up GM card's tag can set difficulty while an unrelated card is credited as 'overcome.'
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Allowed the two fields to diverge: opposition is set by whichever face-up tag(s) fictionally apply (H-03), while 'overcome' credit/leave-play is assigned to the GM card the table narratively agreed was the object of the action (T-02).

ambiguities.issue: The rules require 'The card's owner answers one question from the GM about the filled blank' as a distinct step for each drawn/pulled player card used to fill a Beat Frame blank. The log shows only one GM framing question (event 128, 'Is Ysolde's ferryman already hive-touched...') addressed after both cards (PX-21/Aldous and PX-01/Ysolde) had already surfaced. There is no distinct question-and-answer step visible for Aldous's PX-21 (the WHERE-filling card), and the single question shown references only Ysolde's card.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table treated the single GM framing question in event 128 as satisfying the step-5 requirement collectively for both filled blanks, with Aldous's contribution instead folded into the narrative text of his compel (event 122).

ambiguities.section: §4 (Resolving a drawn player card - compel default vs. power-tag exception)
ambiguities.issue: The compel on PX-21 (event 122) used the power tag 'draws greedy strangers' rather than the card's weakness tag 'Treasure Hunters Turn Violent', invoking the exception that a power tag may be used 'only if that tag causes the trouble directly.' The complication described (armed strangers converging and turning hostile) arguably maps as much or more onto the weakness tag's stated trouble (violence) as onto the power tag (merely drawing attention), making it unclear whether the power-tag exception was properly satisfied rather than the weakness tag being the required default.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table allowed the power-tag compel, reading 'draws greedy strangers' as the direct causal mechanism for the strangers' arrival, and treated any violent escalation as downstream fictional color rather than requiring the weakness tag.

friction.text: No 'GM +1 free invoke' grant rows exist anywhere in the scene 1 log even though T-04 is treated as a face-up GM card used repeatedly as opposition and its tag is invoked once by the GM (event 19) — the log format's own convention for tracking free-invoke legitimacy isn't being followed, making fate-point-economy audits impossible.

GM fate points (gm_fp) never change across the entire scene (stay at 4) despite the GM actively invoking a card tag at event 19 — either that invoke should have cost 1 gm_fp or it should have been logged as a tracked free invoke; as recorded, neither happened, undermining the fate point economy check the engine is supposed to enforce.

The two 'success with style' outcomes (events 17 and 19) both resolve via the Peek option and both leave the same card (L-03) on top of the deck without ever taking a boost or moving it — functionally the mechanic produced two no-op events in a row, which is legal but is a low-value use of the 3+ shifts outcome and may indicate the peek option needs a stronger incentive to actually vary deck order.

Story Pile draws (PS-16) are logged much less rigorously than Session Deck draws: the GM free-invoke grant that the L-03 rail_add explicitly notes is absent for PS-16, and PS-16's scene-cleanup disposition is never logged, making it impossible to confirm the rule was actually applied.

The Beat Frame's required 'owner answers a GM question about the filled blank' step (§5.5) has no dedicated event type in this log format, so compliance can only be inferred from generic roleplay rows, weakening auditability.

The §6A rule that a non-deck compel's complication 'must involve the drawn NPC or move the drawn thread' is structurally hard to satisfy because the Story Pile draw happens only after the compel's complication is already fixed and narrated, creating a built-in sequencing tension the spec doesn't address.

The §6A 'compel not from a deck draw' trigger fires after the compel is already fully narrated and accepted, making it structurally awkward (or impossible, as seen here) to satisfy the requirement that the resulting complication 'must involve the drawn NPC' — the story card arrives too late to shape anything.

Free-invoke grants from card reveals are inconsistently logged: module/rail additions explicitly note 'GM +1 free invoke,' but the PS-14 story draw's rail addition omits this, leaving it unclear whether the GM actually received the invoke §6A requires.

Redundant NPC bookkeeping: 'Ket' is improvised in play and later formalized as a brand-new story card (SN-03) at cleanup's Add step, while the mechanically-drawn PS-14 sits unused on the rail — two cards effectively competing to represent (or not represent) the same scene NPC, with no clear resolution of which one is 'Ket.'

Parallel player declarations (events 98–101) against the same fictional obstacle, resolved sequentially, created a case where one player's success-with-style removed a GM card (T-02) from play mid-resolution while another player's roll (event 109) later still targeted the now-departed card — the spec has no rule for reconciling simultaneous declares against a single target.

The engine's own refusal log flags a Beat Frame/module trigger ('the party leaves the road or causeway') as not matching an unused trigger, echoing the §7 requirement that triggers be observer-checkable; this suggests trigger authoring/matching is a recurring friction point independent of this scene's resolved events.

Divergence between 'target_card' (T-02) and 'opposing_tags' (H-03) on the same rolls makes it hard to audit which GM card's clock should advance or which card is actually being overcome, since §11's clock ruling ties both concepts together ('a roll against a card' = the card's tag set difficulty or was invoked) but the log's fields don't consistently agree on which card that is.

The Beat Frame's required 'owner answers a GM question about the filled blank' step (§5.5) is not clearly logged as a separate event for each pulled card, making it hard to confirm compliance versus it being folded into the compel narration.

Choosing a power tag over the default weakness tag for a compel (event 122) relies on a judgment call about 'direct causation' that the spec doesn't define precisely, inviting inconsistent rulings across tables.

Only 2 of 4 players' cards are shown being pulled for the final-scene backstory guarantee; scene-5-only visibility makes it impossible to confirm from this log alone whether Morwen's and Mire's cards already surfaced earlier in the session as required by the 100% backstory-guarantee target.

free_text.best_moment: The shrine-house ferryman scene. It made concrete the decade of unrepaid kindness Ysolde owed, turning it into a moment of mutual care while holding against the hive's pull. Vulnerable, specific to her character, and collaborative with Morwen's rites.
free_text.most_frustrating: The investigation felt linear (mill → cistern → shrine-house) with limited room to suggest alternate approaches or take real investigative initiative. I followed the GM's breadcrumbs faithfully, which worked, but I wanted more agency in charting the path.
free_text.background_used: Very well. The ferryman and exile threads created authentic emotional weight and real stakes at the toll with Ket. The decade-long debt earned the compel truthfully. Other threads (The Barge That Burned, Teacher's Scrolls) haven't surfaced yet but have space to land.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: More investigative agency—chances to propose *how* to find the hive rather than following the GM's plot path. Some control over whether to help the ferryman rather than having compels decide it, though I recognize that's how compels work.
free_text.one_sentence: Ysolde's background felt genuinely integrated, particularly the ferryman and exile threads, which gave real weight and texture to her choices throughout.

free_text.best_moment: The flood crossing. Aldous's deepest trauma—panic near deep water, marked by drowned ghosts—became his greatest asset when he had to guide everyone across to Tomas. That moment of transmuting terror into power, where "The dead are with me in this water" flipped from something that breaks him into something that saves everyone, felt like genuine character transcendence. The GM let him be broken *and* capable at the same time.
free_text.most_frustrating: I wanted Aldous to escalate toward the source of the hive threat itself rather than continually responding to its effects—to face the Priest or the core directly instead of always rescuing people from what it leaves behind. This isn't a GM failure; it's my preference for head-on escalation clashing with the GM's story structure (symptoms first, source later). Good narrative instinct on their part; just wanted more.
free_text.background_used: Extensively and well. The Sunken Barge (sole survivor, treasure map, ghost-sense), the ferryman's vow, the panic near deep water, the rain-reading—all felt earned and central. The treasure map rumor particularly landed because it came from Aldous's own tavern-mouth, not arbitrarily imposed. Complications from the background created meaningful moments rather than cheap obstacles. The GM used his scars as tools, not punishment.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: More active investigation toward the hive's core and the Priest's motivations. Wanted to use my Contacts skill more directly—to network, dig into underworld knowledge—instead of mostly responding to situations the GM presented. Also wished for clearer insight into what the Priest actually wants beyond "consume everything."
free_text.one_sentence: Aldous's backstory wasn't texture or flavor text—it was the foundation the entire narrative was built on, with vulnerabilities transformed into assets exactly when the story needed them most.

free_text.best_moment: The ferryman scene—when Morwen's rites caught something stubborn in him still fighting the hive's pull, and she anchored him back to himself with ward-signs instead of just diagnosing his doom. It was the perfect expression of her character: she doesn't burn victims or cast them out, she *reaches* for what's still human and holds it steady. That moment crystallized everything about who she is.
free_text.most_frustrating: Nothing substantial. The tie on the cistern Lore roll could have stung, but the GM spent it on a compel that deepened the stakes instead of just negating the discovery. Well done.
free_text.background_used: Extensively and well. The entire back half—cistern investigation, ferryman rescue—was built around hive-victims and Morwen's deep experience surviving the first outbreak. Her knowledge of rites older than the Order felt organic to the story rather than extracted. The way Ket deferred to her as "the Exorcist" and the ferryman's fevered recognition of what she could do: all of it landed. Her background wasn't performed *for* the table; it was woven into why the story needed her.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: Nothing I can point to. I wanted Morwen active in reading the hive-presence itself, and the cistern + ferryman sequences gave me exactly that—investigation and diagnosis and the delicate work of refusing to let the hive have people. Good pacing, good opportunities.
free_text.one_sentence: Morwen's backstory—the trauma, the exorcism, the Sallowmere knowledge, the refusal to burn victims—was central to the session's shape, not grafted on or used against her, and every scene let her live into those themes.

free_text.best_moment: The mill crossing. Mire grabbed Aldous by the shoulder and led everyone through the flood using her personal knowledge of the place and the waterwheel's current-break—it was pure competent tactical action informed by her past, and nobody else could have done it. That's what holding the line actually means.
free_text.most_frustrating: The party's direction was set by NPCs and story momentum—Sella sent us to the mill, Ket guided us to the cistern and shrine-house. Mire responded excellently to each scene, but I never got to *choose* where we were hunting. She had tactical control but not strategic control.
free_text.background_used: The abandoned mill and Sella worked perfectly—organic and earned rather than forced. Mire's militia training and toughness drove her problem-solving the whole session. But the Cartel angle (that Cartel boy who guided the poisoner in) never got pulled, and her disgrace by Verrick and vendetta against the Wardens barely surfaced. Good landing, but could've gone deeper.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: Wanted to pursue the Cartel connection more directly—that boy who guided the poisoner in is exactly Mire's ground to hunt. Also wanted her disgraced Warden status to create more friction or direct confrontation, since "cast out by Captain Verrick" is central to who she is, not just background flavor.
free_text.one_sentence: Mire's background made her the natural tactical leader in crisis moments, but her Cartel debt and personal vendetta didn't get enough activation to feel like they mattered to this story.

chronicle.summary: The party paid Ket's toll in truth, traced a deliberately-poisoned cistern to hive-work matching the Drowned Priest's acolyte markings, and followed a false rumor of silver to a hidden shrine-house — where Ysolde's stranded ferryman lay half-claimed by the hive's song, hooks sunk deep but not yet closed. Working together, Aldous read the wrongness in the water, Morwen anchored the ferryman's failing will with old ward-rites, and Mire sealed the gap in the floor, driving back whatever nested below before it could finish what it started. The thing in the dark went still and watching rather than destroyed — the Stiltfolk's water is safe for tonight, but something patient still waits beneath the shrine-house, and Aldous now carries both a buried debt of gratitude repaid and a fresh crowd of treasure-hunters drawn by his half-charred map.
